{
  "answer": "Chapter IV of the Nigerian Constitution sets out these fundamental rights:\n\n- **Life**, **dignity** (including protection from torture, slavery and forced labour), and **personal liberty**. [fc4e2cbe-dc0e-42e7-a8de-540d4cd639ac, cf89f75d-fa5a-4b13-a607-c2d1950efc44, c8c4bacb-daaf-4588-8b03-b43387004b17]\n- **A fair hearing** and **privacy of your home and communications**. [5dac4c54-e6c8-4ebe-894c-bc785787755f, e5bdbaef-a982-4cef-aa9a-a5e00e05d376]\n- **Freedom of thought, conscience and religion**; **freedom of expression**; and **freedom to assemble and associate with others**. [79599790-5d4f-4ddc-87fa-393c30f556d1, 70eaa7ec-23cc-4a26-9106-34ab692a377b, edec7a6a-1b71-490d-8a31-64e67d95749e]\n- If you are a **Nigerian citizen**, **freedom to move and live anywhere in Nigeria**, **protection from the discrimination specified in section 42**, and **the right to acquire and own immovable property anywhere in Nigeria**. [b5b43f29-8543-4695-aa09-bfdfb936dd9b, 6ddf3333-a1fa-4751-ac36-c1cc6952c89f, 79ef666e-ff27-40a6-a97a-95b84fc5daaa]\n- **Protection against compulsory acquisition of property**, subject to the conditions set out in section 44, including prompt compensation and access to a court or other competent body to determine a compensation claim. [4939f801-a36d-4679-90de-2332869bc21f]\n\nThese rights are not all absolute: the Constitution permits certain restrictions, including laws meeting the conditions in section 45 for privacy, religion, expression, assembly and movement. [fb5bb748-aca4-4e41-ba4d-719d2524e20b] If you believe a Chapter IV right has been, is being, or is likely to be violated in relation to you, section 46 says you may apply to a High Court in the relevant state for redress. [3c88a0cf-40f4-4c77-a8b5-f92df42cb6e7]",
